nodes.name: NCB synthesis by CVD
nodes.procedure: NCB was prepared by a chemical vapor deposition (CVD) method. In the typical synthesis process, 2.0 g 4MgCO3·Mg(OH)2·5H2O was placed in a porcelain boat and heated to 900 °C in a tube furnace with a heating rate of 5 °C min^-1 under 60 sccm N2 flow. A gas-washing bottle containing acetonitrile was connected in the N2 up-stream and the flow rate was reduced to 20 sccm. The CVD process lasted for 3 h at 900 °C, and afterwards the gas-washing bottle was removed. The product powders were washed with 6 M HCl at room temperature for 24 h and dried in a blast oven at 60 °C to obtain nitrogen-functionalized carbon nanobox (NCB).

nodes.name: NiSA RuAC@NCB synthesis
nodes.procedure: 2.37 mg NiCl2·6H2O, 4.14 mg RuCl3 and 20 mg NCB were dissolved in 10 mL deionized water, and then stirred at room temperature for 24 h. The mixture was then filtered and freeze-dried. The obtained solid was calcined at 500 °C for 1 h under Ar atmosphere with a heating rate of 10 °C min^-1.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images and EDS mapping prove isolated atom configuration of Ni/Ru in precursor at 25°C, Ru atoms agglomerate into subnanometer Ru_AC at 100°C while Ni remains as stable Ni_SA, higher temperatures increase Ru_AC size but Ni stays monatomic.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1b, high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image and corresponding energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping prove the isolated atom configuration of Ni/Ru in the precursor (25 °C). ... The higher temperature of 300 °C and 500 °C further increased the RuAC size yet still cannot induce the clustering of NiSA.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge EXAFS shows only Ni-N bond at ~1.5 Å with no Ni-Ni bond; Ru K-edge shows Ru-Ru bond at ~2.4 Å confirming Ru clustering.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni K-edge EXAFS spectrum displays only a pronounced nearest-neighbor peaks at ca. 1.5 Å ascribed to Ni–N bond, whereas the Ni-Ni bond is totally absent. ... Ru K-edge EXAFS spectrum displays the characteristic peak of Ru-Ru at ca. 2.4 Å, suggesting the clustering of Ru atoms into multi-atom aggregate.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDS mapping/line scans confirm bimetallic SA-SA, AC-AC, and SA-AC configurations for various metal pairs on NCB based on cohesive energy differences.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2b–d show the HAADF-STEM, and EDS mapping/line scans of the obtained bimetallic SA/AC composites. ... For nine type-ii M-Ru bimetal pairs, clear Ru clusters can be observed both in HAADF-STEM images and EDS mappings for all specimens.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images and EDS line scans verify coexistence of Ru_AC clusters and isolated Fe/Co/Ni_SA atoms with spatial overlapping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HAADF-STEM images (Fig. 4a) and EDS line scans (Fig. S15) verified the coexistence of RuAC and isolated (Fe/Co/Ni)SA.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3p peaks shift ~0.3 eV to lower binding energy in M_SA Ru_AC @ NCB compared to Ru_AC @ NCB, indicating different oxidation states and interactions between Ru_AC and M_SA-modified substrates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4b shows the Ru 3p spectra with spin-orbit split Ru 3p3/2 and Ru 3p1/2 peaks. Compared to M_SA-free Ru_AC@NCB, the Ru 3p positions for M_SA Ru_AC@NCB display shift of around 0.3 eV to the lower binding energy.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES pre-edge spectra close to Ru foil indicate metallic state of Ru_AC; varying white line intensities show different charge densities around Ru_AC due to M_SA interaction; Fe/Co/Ni K-edge confirm positive valence states in M_SA-N-C moieties.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Per Fig. 4c, the pre-edge spectra of Ru in M_SA Ru_AC@NCB are close to Ru foil, indicating the metallic state of RuAC with enriched electron density. ... The XANES of Fe K-edge, Co K-edge and Ni K-edge (Fig. 4d) verify the positive valence states of single atom Fe, Co and Ni in M_SA–N–C moieties.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge EXAFS shows Ru-Ru at ~2.4 Å and Ru-N at ~1.5 Å; Fe/Co/Ni EXAFS show only M-N at ~1.5 Å with no M-M peaks, confirming single atom configuration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 4e, two characteristic peaks locate at ca. 2.4 Å and 1.5 Å being attributed to Ru-Ru and Ru-N bonding, respectively... Regarding to the Fe/Co/Ni species in M_SA Ru_AC@NCB, the EXAFS spectra of Fe/Co/Ni in R space display the pronounced nearest-neighbor peaks at ca. 1.5 Å (M-N) and the absence of M-M peaks.

nodes.characterization_summary: Septenary high-entropy single atom material Fe_SA·Co_SA·Ni_SA·Cr_SA·Mn_SA·Cu_SA·Pd_SA @ NCB shows total metal loading of 20.49 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The loading of each metal is fairly high leading to the total loading of 20.49 wt% (Table S3), which is the highest loading of high-entropy single atom materials reported to date.

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS mapping identifies isolated dark spots as Ru clusters during in-situ heating.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With increasing temperature, isolated dark spots gradually appeared on the margins of NCBs, which can be all identified as Ru clusters by electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) mapping.
